SWS-SEND.interpretation: August2022 section3.8.6.2.1 MUST-38 and recommended send rules: fixed MSS4, Fs=1/2, maximum accepted send window per connection. A selected normal new-data prefix must be full MSS, all queued pushed data, at least half the maximum window, or timeout-authorized. The latter still obeys receiver/congestion budgets and the independent parent Nagle gate.

SWS-TIMEOUT.interpretation: Separate override timer configurable100..1000ms, default200. First pending transmit/accepted-ACK/push/close request starts the epoch. More writes or repeat requests do not postpone it. Expiry grants a zero-time choice opportunity and retained readiness, never directly sends; actual first-send progress starts the next remaining-queue epoch. Cleanup cancels. Probes/retransmissions keep parent behavior.

SWS-PUSH.interpretation: app.push marks only the current queued prefix, not later writes, and grants a finite send opportunity in ESTABLISHED/CLOSE-WAIT. Closing marks its queued prefix similarly. This is application coalescing intent; wire PSH is outside the present message schema.

SWS-SCOPE.interpretation: Pinned RFC version/source hashes and declared policy. No dynamic MSS, window scaling, wire PSH, lwIP special send-queue variations, Linux evidence or universal implementation refinement.
